name: Laon

art.title: The Neumark Dragoons at Athies, Laon

summary: Blücher, with twice Napoleon's numbers, held the hill of Laon against him; on the night of the 9th Yorck and Kleist fell on Marmont's corps at Athies and routed it, and Napoleon, attacking again next day to no purpose, withdrew.

forces.name: Meunier's Division
forces.summary: Ney's first Young Guard division, under eight hundred men after Craonne, in the attacks on the hill of Laon from the south-west on the 9th and 10th.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.
Nafziger's Laon return gives only the army's divisions; their units are from his Craonne return two days before, and Marmont's from his return of the VI Corps on 12 March.
The division was down to 865 men; its eight battalions are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.
Its regiments were newly raised that winter, largely of conscripts under a cadre of veterans; they are the list's Young Guard, as it rates them.
Battalion numbers, brigades and guns, which this return leaves out, are as at La Rothière.
Its foot battery, with four battalions in its brigade, where the list wants six for one, shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Boyer de Rébeval's Division
forces.summary: The division of Victor's corps, now without Victor, in the attacks on Laon from the south-west.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
Nafziger's Laon return gives only the army's divisions; their units are from his Craonne return two days before, and Marmont's from his return of the VI Corps on 12 March.
The division had 3,800 men in eleven battalions.

Nafziger gives these line battalions to Boyer de Rébeval as Victor's 9th Division, and Pierre Boyer a division of unknown battalions under Ney. Wikipedia's account has it the other way about: Pierre Boyer's 9th Division with Ney, and Boyer de Rébeval a provisional Young Guard division of conscripts with Victor. This follows Nafziger.
Its two foot batteries, eight 6-pdrs and four howitzers, are one in its divisional artillery and one in its reserve, as the list takes them.
Brigades of four regiments, where the list's take three, and two light regiments, where it allows one in the division, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

Lion's brigade was the chasseurs, about five hundred, and the Empress Dragoons, about seven hundred; Letort's the grenadiers, about eight hundred and fifty. The dragoons are with Letort's grenadiers here, as the list's heavy brigade takes them.

Nafziger brigades the fusiliers together, each with a vélite battalion, and the flanqueurs with Gros; the vélites are the list's Italian brigade here. The Flanqueurs-Chasseurs and Flanqueurs-Grenadiers are the list's Tirailleurs.

forces.name: Ricard's Division
forces.summary: Marmont's division on the Berry-au-Bac road, which came up to Athies on the 9th. In the night Yorck's and Kleist's Prussians fell on Marmont's bivouacs and routed the corps, taking forty-five guns; Fabvier's men and an Old Guard escort kept the road back open.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's return of Marmont's corps on 12 March, two days after Laon and the rout at Athies, from the French archives.
After Athies the division had about 650 men in seven battalions, fifty to a hundred and sixty each. They are shown at full size; the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.
Nafziger gives the battalions without brigades; they are split here, light and line, as the list takes them.
A brigade of four light battalions, where the list takes three regiments and one light regiment in the division, shows as a historical departure.

forces.name: Lagrange's Division
forces.summary: Marmont's other division, with Ricard's at Athies when the Prussians fell on the corps in the night of the 9th; Marmont lost forty-five guns and the corps fell back in disorder.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.
After Nafziger's return of Marmont's corps on 12 March, two days after Laon and the rout at Athies, from the French archives.
Its marine regiments were sailors and naval gunners of the fleet's artillery, brought inland in 1813; they fought well, and are shown as Line, the list's Veteran upgrade would suit them.

Nafziger gives the division as one brigade; its regiments are brigaded here as at La Rothière, after Nafziger's history as Wikipedia's order of battle has it. Battalion numbers he leaves out, and the division's artillery, are from his returns of 25 January and La Rothière.
Nafziger gives the 37th Line, but it is the 37th Léger, which served in the division at Leipzig; the 37th Line was in Duhesme's division of Victor's corps.
After Athies the division had about 1,400 men in twenty-one battalions; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.

Nafziger gives Marmont's artillery on this return only as a foot and a horse company of January; the batteries here are those of the 25 January return. Clavel's four regiments, where the list's brigade takes three, show as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.

Nafziger's Laon return gives Arrighi the I Cavalry Corps and the 2nd Paris Reserve Division; his 12 March return calls it the 1st Division of the Paris Reserve, with a provisional cavalry brigade of the I Cavalry Corps.

The division had about 1,800 men in twelve battalions, and the cavalry about 1,600 in four provisional regiments. Nafziger gives the infantry without brigades; it is split between two here, in his order.
The provisional regiments are as at La Rothière, a hussar regiment and three of chasseurs, made up from the squadrons left at the depots of many regiments.

forces.name: Yorck's Corps
forces.summary: Blücher's eastern wing, which with Kleist's corps fell on Marmont's bivouacs at Athies in the night of the 9th and routed his corps, Jürgass's horse riding through the camps and taking forty-five guns.
notes: Built from Albion Triumphant's Prussian 1815 list, the nearest to 1814: its Prussian Infantry Brigade is the brigade of 1813 and 1814, the size of another army's division, with line, reserve and Landwehr battalions.
After Nafziger's order of battle for the allied army at Laon, from Damitz's history and the Prussian archives.
A Prussian brigade was the size of another army's division, so the whole corps is here. Take the brigades you want; each is a force in itself.

Battalions of different regiments that served together are grouped as a regiment, as the list takes them. Reserve battalions are the list's Musketeers; grenadier battalions are Musketeers with its Veteran upgrade.
Brigades of three regiments or more have a Subordinate Commander, named where the order of battle names the brigade's infantry commander.
After a month's fighting several brigades had been put together, and their weakest battalions into combined ones; each combined battalion is shown as one unit.

Nafziger gives the 2nd East Prussian's two battalions as one regiment; the one here is grouped with the Brandenburg regiment, as the list takes three regiments in a brigade. The East Prussian National Cavalry, a volunteer regiment, and the Silesian Landwehr cavalry are the list's Mounted Landwehr.
Schmidt's corps artillery is the list's reserve, with a horse battery with each cavalry brigade.
More cavalry, reserve artillery and Schützen than the list allows for the corps' brigades, regiments of more battalions than it takes, and brigades without Landwehr, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

Nafziger gives only the 9th and 10th Brigades; the 11th and 12th, broken at Vauchamps, are not on his return. The 6th Reserve's third battalion was at Erfurt. The 10th Brigade's three combined battalions aren't named.

Braun's corps artillery is the list's reserve, with a horse battery with each regular cavalry brigade.
More cavalry, reserve artillery and Schützen than the list allows for the corps' brigades, regiments of more battalions than it takes, and brigades without Landwehr, show as historical departures.

notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Russian list, which covers 1812-15.

Krasovsky's 15th Division, the 14th and 15th Jäger with three batteries, and Benckendorff's detachment of the Pavlograd Hussars and Bug Cossacks; Harpe's brigade, with Vorontsov's corps at Craonne, isn't on the Laon return.
Three batteries with two battalions, where the list allows none, and no infantry brigade to allow the Jäger and cavalry, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces; but 1 of the 2 brigade commanders at 7, as the list rates at most half of them higher.
